outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: AI-monetizing cloud and enterprise software, led by Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and ServiceNow
strongest.reason: cloud-earnings momentum is extending into a new week, an expanded Oracle-Google Cloud AI partnership is drawing fresh attention, and ServiceNow raised its full-year guidance after a standout quarter
a blowout Q2 report with 93% revenue growth and a big guidance raise sent the stock sharply higher and reinforced the broader application-layer AI software rebound

weakest.reason: a broad chip-sector selloff tied to AI-infrastructure spending-sustainability worries, weak Samsung preliminary results, and Chinese competition headlines dragged AMD and Micron lower even as AMD reported earnings after today's close
bitcoin and ethereum both fell further today as a hardware-wallet key-security exploit added a fresh negative catalyst on top of an already consolidating market

outlook.nextStep: AMD's after-the-close report lands right in the middle of a jittery chip sector, so how it's received against an already-priced 8-9% swing is worth a closer look tomorrow. The broader AI-infrastructure spending-sustainability debate driving today's semiconductor selloff looks like a bigger multi-week swing factor than any single print, and is probably better watched across the rest of this earnings-heavy week than acted on today.

signals.title: Fed holds steady with dissent as oil extends its slide
signals.body: The Fed kept rates unchanged in July with three officials dissenting in favor of a hike, and most members now project little to no further move through year-end. Separately, crude extended a sharp multi-day slide as progress in US-Iran talks continues to ease the war-risk premium.
signals.focus: better watched than acted on given the split committee

signals.title: Cloud and AI-partnership momentum keeps building
signals.body: Oracle jumped on news of an expanded AI partnership with Google Cloud, while Microsoft and Amazon both extended recent gains ahead of a heavy week of cloud-related earnings and AI-spending commentary.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how durable the cloud-acceleration narrative proves this week

signals.title: Broad AI-spending-sustainability selloff hits chips as AMD reports
signals.body: A wide semiconductor selloff, tied to renewed worries about whether hyperscaler AI capex is sustainable, weak Samsung preliminary results, and Chinese competitive threats, pulled Micron and AMD sharply lower even as Nvidia recovered into the green. AMD's Q2 report lands after today's close with an 8-9% swing already priced in.
signals.focus: better watched than acted on until the AI-capex debate and AMD's print settle out

signals.title: Tesla keeps leaning into Optimus production
signals.body: Tesla shares extended their recent gain as the company continues converting factory capacity toward humanoid-robot production, with management still targeting public Optimus sales by late 2027.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how the production timeline holds up

signals.title: Palantir's blowout quarter headlines a software rebound
signals.body: Palantir surged after reporting 93% revenue growth and raising full-year guidance well above prior estimates, driven by triple-digit US commercial growth. The move adds to a broader enterprise-software rebound, with ServiceNow also raising guidance after a standout quarter.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether the software rebound has legs beyond today's earnings pop

signals.title: Wallet-security exploit adds fresh pressure to a soft crypto market
signals.body: Bitcoin and ethereum both extended their pullback as researchers flagged a third wave of fund sweeps tied to weak Coldcard-generated keys, adding a security-driven catalyst on top of an already consolidating market.
signals.focus: lower conviction right now until the wallet-security issue is better understood

signals.title: Cybersecurity names extend their run
signals.body: CrowdStrike and Zscaler both pushed higher again, continuing to build on last week's threat-intelligence report and new European sovereign-cloud partnership, respectively.
signals.focus: worth a closer look given the string of positive fundamental catalysts
